title: Ridge Regression with ridge
text: ridge package provides tools fitting working ridge regression models. includes model fitting, cross-validation selecting regularization parameter, graphical visualization cross-validation errors, prediction methods. vignette presents complete reproducible workflow using main functions S3 methods implemented package.

title: Ridge Regression with ridge
text: Ridge regression regularized linear regression method designed reduce magnitude regression coefficients. estimator minimizes following penalized least-squares criterion: β̂λ=argminβ[∑=1n(yi−β0−xi⊤β)2+λ∑j=1pβj2]. \widehat{\beta}_{\lambda} = \arg\min_{\beta} \left[ \sum_{=1}^{n} (y_i-\beta_0-x_i^\top\beta)^2 + \lambda\sum_{j=1}^{p}\beta_j^2 \right]. , λ\lambda controls strength regularization. larger value λ\lambda produces stronger shrinkage explanatory-variable coefficients. intercept penalized implementation used package.

title: Ridge Regression with ridge
text: generate simulated dataset two explanatory variables known underlying linear relationship. data-generating process : Yi=2+3Xi1−Xi2+εi, Y_i = 2 + 3X_{i1} - X_{i2} + \varepsilon_i, error term follows standard normal distribution. theoretical coefficients therefore 2 intercept, 3 first explanatory variable, -1 second.
code: set.seed(123)  x <- matrix(rnorm(200), ncol = 2) colnames(x) <- c("x1", "x2")  y <- 2 + 3 * x[, 1] - x[, 2] + rnorm(100)

title: Ridge Regression with ridge
text: ridge_fit() function fits ridge regression model specified regularization parameter. resulting object belongs S3 class ridge_model. estimated coefficients can compared theoretical values used generate data.

title: Ridge Regression with ridge
text: ridge_cv() function performs k-fold cross-validation user-defined grid regularization parameters. consider 50 values lambda distributed logarithmic scale. selected parameter minimizes estimated mean cross-validation error specified grid.
code: lambda_grid <- 10^seq(-3, 2, length.out = 50)  cv_result <- ridge_cv(   x = x,   y = y,   lambda_grid = lambda_grid,   k = 5,   seed = 123 )  cv_result$best_lambda #> [1] 0.08685114 cv_result$best_mse #> [1] 0.9270251

title: Ridge Regression with ridge
text: S3 plotting method displays mean cross-validation error function lambda, together standard error selected regularization parameters.  Two selection criteria considered: minimum-error criterion selects lambda associated smallest estimated cross-validation error. one-standard-error rule selects largest lambda whose estimated error remains within one standard error minimum. latter favors stronger regularization accepting cross-validation error close minimum.
code: selected_parameters <- plot(cv_result) selected_parameters #>    lambda_min    lambda_1se     min_error        se_min threshold_1se  #>    0.08685114    7.54312006    0.92702508    0.08993552    1.01696061

title: Ridge Regression with ridge
text: fit two models using parameters selected two criteria. Euclidean norms explanatory-variable coefficients can used illustrate shrinkage induced regularization.
code: model_min <- ridge_fit(   x = x,   y = y,   lambda = selected_parameters["lambda_min"] )  model_1se <- ridge_fit(   x = x,   y = y,   lambda = selected_parameters["lambda_1se"] )  comparison <- cbind(   Theoretical = c(2, 3, -1),   Lambda_min = coef(model_min),   Lambda_1se = coef(model_1se) )  comparison #>             Theoretical Lambda_min Lambda_1se #> (Intercept)           2  2.1354178  2.1633122 #> x1                    3  2.8638539  2.6296842 #> x2                   -1 -0.9754127 -0.9128905 beta_min <- coef(model_min)[-1] beta_1se <- coef(model_1se)[-1]  sqrt(sum(beta_min^2)) #> [1] 3.025407 sqrt(sum(beta_1se^2)) #> [1] 2.783632

title: Ridge Regression with ridge
text: predict() method allows predictions obtained new observations. can also compare training mean squared errors two selected models. training errors describe fit observations used model estimation. interpreted independent estimates predictive performance.
code: newdata <- x[1:5, , drop = FALSE]  predict(model, newdata = newdata) #> [1] 1.238475 1.238511 6.793456 2.675014 3.425870 pred_min <- predict(model_min, newdata = x) pred_1se <- predict(model_1se, newdata = x)  mse_min <- mean((y - pred_min)^2) mse_1se <- mean((y - pred_1se)^2)  data.frame(   Model = c("Minimum CV", "One-standard-error rule"),   Lambda = c(     selected_parameters["lambda_min"],     selected_parameters["lambda_1se"]   ),   Training_MSE = c(mse_min, mse_1se) ) #>                              Model     Lambda Training_MSE #> lambda_min              Minimum CV 0.08685114    0.8778267 #> lambda_1se One-standard-error rule 7.54312006    0.9292174

text: Ridge Regression estimates coefficients minimizing: 𝛃̂λ=argminβ0,𝛃[∑=1n(yi−β0−𝐱⊤𝛃)2+λ∑j=1pβj2]. \widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_\lambda = \arg\min_{\beta_0,\boldsymbol{\beta}} \left[ \sum_{=1}^{n} (y_i-\beta_0-\mathbf{x}_i^\top\boldsymbol{\beta})^2 + \lambda\sum_{j=1}^{p}\beta_j^2 \right]. intercept penalized.

title: Ridge Regression Tools
text: ridge_cv() function performs K-fold cross-validation grid candidate regularization parameters.
code: lambda_grid <- 10^seq(-3, 2, length.out = 50)  cv_result <- ridge_cv(   x,   y,   lambda_grid = lambda_grid,   k = 5,   seed = 123 )  cv_result$best_lambda cv_result$best_mse

title: Ridge Regression Tools
text: package calculates two complementary criteria. pooled cross-validation error : CVpooled(λ)=1n∑k=1K∑∈Vk(yi−ŷ(−k))2. CV_{\mathrm{pooled}}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^{K} \sum_{\V_k} (y_i-\widehat y_i^{(-k)})^2. mean fold cross-validation error : CVfold(λ)=1K∑k=1KEk(λ), CV_{\mathrm{fold}}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} E_k(\lambda), Ek(λ)E_k(\lambda) mean squared prediction error validation fold kk. best_lambda returned ridge_cv() minimizes pooled cross-validation error.

title: Ridge Regression Tools
text: plot provides two selection criteria: lambda_min: minimizes mean fold cross-validation error. lambda_1se: selects largest lambda whose mean fold error within one estimated standard error minimum. criteria based mean fold errors may differ best_lambda, uses pooled criterion. plotting method invisibly returns selected parameters:
code: plot(cv_result) selected_parameters <- plot(cv_result)  selected_parameters
